target.title: fix(discord): use grapheme-cluster-aware chunk splitting for ZWJ emoji
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord chunking used surrogate-pair-level code-point boundary detection via `isHighSurrogate`/`isLowSurrogate`, which only protects individual emoji encoded as a single surrogate pair (two UTF-16 code units). Multi-codepoint grapheme clusters — such as ZWJ sequences like 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 (family: 7 codepoints / 11 UTF-16 units), emoji with skin-tone modifiers, or flag sequences — could be split across Discord message chunks, producing broken rendering in the Discord client.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replaces `clampToCodePointBoundary` with `clampToGraphemeBoundary` that uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to split on true grapheme cluster boundaries.
- Removes the now-unused `isHighSurrogate` helper.
- Retains `isLowSurrogate` for a pre-check that adjusts the candidate index when it lands on a trailing surrogate, so `text.slice(0, index)` never produces a dangling surrogate before the Segmenter pass.

## User Impact

- ZWJ emoji sequences (e.g. 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦, 🏃‍♂️) and other multi-codepoint grapheme clusters are kept intact across Discord message chunks.
- No change for single-codepoint characters or existing surrogate-pair emoji.
- All 17 existing chunk tests continue to pass.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts` — 17 passed
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts`
- `git diff --check`
